literal: not killing, it has the goodness, penance; others' fault, not saying, it has the goodness, perfection.
translation: Penance has the goodness of not killing. Perfection has the goodness of not speaking of others' faults.
modern: உயிர்களைக் கொல்லாத நற்பண்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டது தவம். அதுபோல, மற்றவர்களின் குற்றங்களைச் சொல்லாத நற்பண்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டது சான்றாண்மை.
explanation: This couplet defines the core virtues of two great ideals: penance and perfection. True penance (நோன்மை) is rooted in the goodness of not harming or killing any living being. Similarly, true perfection or nobility (சால்பு) is rooted in the goodness of not speaking about the faults of others. By placing these two side by side, the poet elevates the social virtue of refraining from gossip to the same level as the ascetic virtue of non-violence.
